studies.name: BASS-II / PMMA rods
studies.objective: Study opposed flame spread over cylindrical PMMA under different oxygen, flow and gravity conditions.
studies.configuration: Opposed flow; Earth ground tests and ISS microgravity
studies.conditions: Oxygen, diameter and imposed flow. Per-run pressure is unresolved.
studies.hardware: ISS Microgravity Science Glovebox, SPICE-derived flow duct. Ground tests used separate equipment.
studies.available: 69 modeled records: 35 Earth means + 34 ISS segments
studies.limits: 11 ISS rates retain an inferred-unit flag. Shared specimen grouping is provisional. No validated lunar predictor.
studies.utility: Compare within-environment rate estimates and identify where physics or Earth-to-ISS transfer fails.

sources.locator: Appendix A, PDF p114 / printed p106

studies.name: FLEX
studies.objective: Investigate droplet combustion and inert-gas suppressant mixtures in microgravity.
studies.configuration: ISS microgravity; recorded O2 / N2 / CO2 / He mixtures
studies.measurement: Average slope magnitude of droplet diameter squared versus time
studies.conditions: Initial diameter, pressure in mmHg and gas mole fractions.
studies.hardware: Multi-User Droplet Combustion Apparatus / Combustion Integrated Rack
studies.available: 198 eligible / 274 source CSV records; 79 condition groups
studies.limits: Rate model only; no extinction probability, causal suppressant ranking or dose recommendation. Disrupted trials excluded.
studies.utility: Compare measured burning constants with held-out estimates and inspect the largest errors across recorded mixtures.

sources.locator: K definition PDF p25; Table IX pp26–34

studies.name: SAME / SAME-R
studies.objective: Study smoke aerosols relevant to spacecraft detection.
studies.material: Smoke-producing samples; material and aging conditions in the local tables
studies.configuration: Microgravity smoke experiments; aging and inlet conditions vary
studies.measurement: Local files describe experiment settings, not paired detector-response labels
studies.conditions: SAME: material, airflow, weight-loss setting, aging. SAME-R: material, inlet velocity, duration and aging.
studies.hardware: Smoke aerosol measurement instrumentation; full sensor-response files needed. The modified P-Trak counts aerosol particles. DAFT tested its operation for SAME.
studies.available: 8 SAME design-summary rows; 109 SAME-R metadata records
studies.limits: Aged measurements can share a test. The SAME-R date field omits the year. No accepted smoke/dust classifier dataset.
studies.utility: Find relevant smoke studies and identify the response measurements required before detector modeling.

studies.name: LUCI
studies.objective: Examine material burning at lunar-like gravity produced by vehicle rotation.
studies.material: 4 mm PMMA rod and cotton/fiberglass fabric sheet
studies.configuration: Rotating suborbital vehicle; lunar-like acceleration, not the lunar surface
studies.measurement: Flame growth/spread reference fits from camera observations
studies.units: mm/s for curated reference fits; different target definitions
studies.conditions: Changing chamber oxygen; orientation and Coriolis effects matter.
studies.hardware: Rotating New Shepard payload; two orthogonal cameras
studies.available: 6 separately curated reference values; not 6 independent tests
studies.limits: Upward tip/base growth is not opposed leading-edge spread. Not a compatible answer key for our PMMA model.
studies.utility: Identify real partial-gravity evidence and explain the target-matching gap before lunar validation.

applications.name: Moon base and pressurized rover
applications.question: Does our rod model cover an exploration cabin?
applications.finding: The 34% O₂, 8.2 psi example exceeds measured oxygen coverage on Earth (17.5–20.9%) and the ISS (17.0–20.8%). Individual rod pressures are unresolved.
applications.limit: A matched experiment needs pressure, oxygen, gravity, diameter, opposed flow and a leading-edge spread rate. The Earth and ISS measurements cannot bound a lunar or Martian rate.
applications.context: The brief describes a 4.3 psi oxygen suit and oxygen pre-breathing to remove nitrogen. Possible cabins at ≥30% oxygen and ≤10.2 psi introduce a separate material-testing question.

applications.name: Burner feed and cabin oxygen
applications.question: Where was the high oxygen concentration applied?
applications.finding: In the challenge’s inverse-flame example, up to 85% oxygen flows out of a spherical burner into nitrogen and fuel gas.
applications.limit: That percentage describes an inlet stream. It provides no cabin flammability threshold or PMMA spread rate.
applications.context: Oxygen feed → spherical burner → chamber containing nitrogen and fuel gas.

applications.name: Smoke detection on Earth
applications.question: Can a detector distinguish smoke from dust?
applications.finding: NASA documents a shuttle-derived fire detector that discriminated smoke from dust to reduce nuisance alarms. SAME and DAFT provide related particle-measurement evidence.
applications.limit: Scoring false alarms requires paired exposure, detector response and event labels. The local experimental settings alone cannot supply that score.
applications.context: Compare number concentration with the response of a detector exposed to the same aerosol.

applications.name: Fire suppression and protective equipment
applications.question: What could inform terrestrial fire protection?
applications.finding: The challenge gives fine water mist as a suppression example. FLEX measures the burning constant of individual droplets in recorded gas mixtures.
applications.limit: Mist performance requires a measured suppression outcome under defined application conditions. FLEX K alone cannot rank extinguishers or select a dose.
applications.context: NASA separately documents spacesuit technology adapted to firefighters’ breathing equipment and protective clothing.

sources.locator: NASA Spinoff · New Technology for the Fire Attire
